title: Silverfish 🐛 House Centipede Series Part 5
tiktok_title: Silverfish: Fossils From 400 Million Years Ago, Weak Jaws and a Mating Dance
tiktok_caption: silverfish 🐛 part 5 of our house centipede series. Will it bite you? It has very weak jaws, so it scrapes the surface of paper instead of biting it, and silverfish do not transmit disease. Its fossils date to 400 million years ago, about twice as long ago as the dinosaurs. It moves fast, even sideways. Males do a mating dance with antennae and head wagging, and a silverfish can pass through 45 to 60 stages in its life. The house centipede you just met eats these. More on YouTube, Meatball Myths. Sources: Missouri Department of Conservation, UC IPM (University of California), Penn State Extension, University of Maryland Extension. Squish it or let it live? #silverfish #bugsinhouse #thingslivinginyourhouse #insects #housebugs

rows: SQUISH IT OR LET IT LIVE?

beats.say: It has very weak jaws, so it scrapes the surface of paper instead of biting it. And they do not transmit disease.
Its fossils date to 400 million years ago. That's about twice as long ago as the dinosaurs. Meatball's lunch is not that old. Probably.
They move rapidly, including sideways, and their flat bodies let them hide in narrow crevices. Meatball can't even walk sideways.
Males attract females with a mating dance, antennae contact and head wagging, then leave a sperm capsule for her to pick up. Meatball's last date just got a breadstick.
The babies look like the adults, only whitish and much smaller, and they have no scales at first.
It can pass through 45 to 60 stages, or instars, in its life. Meatball's list goes baby, kid, snack.
Silverfish live about 3 years. In some species, individuals can live for 8 years. That's longer than Meatball's houseplant.
They can invade new homes from wild areas nearby, especially as those areas dry out in summer. They can also come in on lumber and wallboard.
And the house centipede you just met eats these. So, squish it, or let it live?
